rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 5 headers. 4 of 5 are claim-shaped: 'Plan review is a high-leverage gate' (line 29) and 'What you can test and check sets your complexity ceiling' (line 35) are load-bearing declaratives naming the mechanism, matching the rule's binding clause for law/consolidation slides; 'Five things a good plan has' (line 15) and 'Three pressures that make bad plans look good' (line 23) are catalogue entries naming their subject, the rule's own NOT-violation category. Closest call: chunk 1 'Ask plan mode what changed' (line 9) is grammatically imperative, not a claim — the shape rule 15 keeps to exercises by default. The maintainer block (line 59) documents this as deliberate: 'Header is a do-move imperative (`check_lectures §4` live-do carve-out); the prompt stays student-run (`check_lectures §6` answer-must-be-theirs carve-out...)'. check_slides §15 names no carve-out of its own for this exact shape (only orientation/catalogue/phase-label), so this is an accept-note-backed judgment call rather than a clean rule match. The harm §15 exists to prevent — diluting the lecture-vs-exercise mood switch so a genuine declarative-inside-an-exercise beat stops standing out — is absent: this is a lecture with ONE imperative header for a single, explicitly-justified live-do beat, and every other header is claim-shaped. Not filed as REVISE. Non-blocking: a mismatched header grammar on one slide costs polish, not comprehension — the slide is still followable, same family as rule 6.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 16 body bullets across chunks 2-5 (chunk 1 has zero bullets, prompt-only) against the three low-value classes. No doctrine restatement — each bullet adds a new move, example, or causal link rather than re-announcing an already-landed lens (e.g. chunk 5 line 41 'Reach without calibration is what the three pressures produce' draws a NEW causal link between two previously separate ideas rather than repeating either). No self-referential design commentary — no line tells the student it is inside a pedagogy. No aphorism kicker — no bullet closes a slide by restating its own header. Closest candidate: chunk 5 line 43, 'The ceiling is not fixed. Every check you make cheap and repeatable raises it, so building a better check buys you more than approving a bigger plan.' — reads kicker-shaped (closes the deck) but the maintainer block confirms it is deliberately load-bearing new content ('The last bullet carries the raise', line 51), not a restatement of the header. Second-closest: chunk 5 line 42, 'Push reach past what you can check and you have not delegated more. You are checking less.' — introduces a genuine new distinction (delegating vs. checking), not stated earlier. Non-blocking: a low-value bullet wastes attention but doesn't block comprehension, same family as rule 7's non-superlative sub-items.
